final_briefs.title: Kodeida
final_briefs.description: **Turn coding practice into a pixel‑art adventure.** Kodeida is a pre‑alpha offline game where you write Python, JavaScript or TypeScript to move the hero through worlds inspired by Ukrainian literature. It blends LeetCode‑style challenges with a story‑driven UI, letting beginners experiment with real code while exploring fairy‑tale settings. The project ships with a downloadable release, a trailer, and a website for easy access.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Turns learning LeetCode patterns into a playable adventure, letting beginners practice Python, JavaScript or TypeScript without leaving the game.
final_briefs.who_cares: Novice programmers and educators looking for an engaging, offline way to teach coding fundamentals.

final_briefs.title: Open‑Source Radar
final_briefs.description: **Find a fresh, beginner‑friendly issue and turn it into a merged pull request.** This open‑source project curates unclaimed issues from active repositories, refreshed every 12 hours, and groups them by language and topic. It also bundles a step‑by‑step contribution guide and even publishes the dataset on Hugging Face. As of the latest update there are 3,369 open issues, 1,273 labeled for beginners, and 1,149 active projects.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Aggregates fresh, beginner‑friendly issues from active projects and bundles a step‑by‑step contribution guide, cutting the guesswork out of open‑source onboarding.
final_briefs.who_cares: First‑time contributors, mentors, and maintainers who want to surface easy wins for the community.

final_briefs.title: Atticus (macOS)
final_briefs.description: **A Claude‑powered voice assistant that runs locally on your Mac without any API keys.** Hold ⌃⌥Space, speak a command, and Atticus can move windows, open apps, search the web, draw diagrams, and even dictate text. It learns shortcuts as you use it, runs background agents for heavy tasks, and keeps all voice data on‑device for privacy. Installation is a one‑liner script, and it works with Claude Pro, Claude Max, or other local models.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: A Claude‑powered voice assistant that runs locally on macOS, learns your shortcuts, and can control windows, files, and the web without any API keys.
final_briefs.who_cares: Mac power users and developers who want AI‑driven automation while keeping everything on their machine.

final_briefs.title: REA (Reverse Engineer Anything)
final_briefs.description: **A modular MCP‑based framework for reverse‑engineering binaries, applications, and runtime behavior.** REA ships as an npm package (`rea‑agents`) and provides a catalog of pluggable agents that can dissect code down to the binary level. It supports dozens of languages for its documentation and is licensed under MIT. The project also offers a Discord community for collaboration.
final_briefs.why_it_matters: Offers a modular MCP‑based framework for reverse‑engineering binaries, apps, and runtime behavior, automating tedious analysis with pluggable agents.
final_briefs.who_cares: Security researchers, reverse‑engineers, and devs building tooling around binary analysis.

final_briefs.title: WinShun
final_briefs.description: **Press Ctrl twice and search your entire Windows PC—everything from files to clipboard history.** WinShun is a free, open‑source launcher that combines pinyin file search, full‑text indexing of Word/Excel/PDF, clipboard history with OCR, task‑bar search, and an AI assistant MCP. It bundles eleven tools in one package and runs on Windows 10 | 11 (x64).
final_briefs.why_it_matters: A single‑press Windows launcher that combines pinyin file search, full‑text document indexing, clipboard history with OCR, and an AI assistant—all free and open source.
final_briefs.who_cares: Windows power users and developers who need a fast, extensible replacement for Spotlight/Listary.
